raw:
Let me analyze this request. The user wants Japanese UI copy for an EC (e-commerce) app:

- s1: Message shown on the cart screen when the cart is empty (there's already a "商品を探す" (Find products) button at the bottom of the screen)
- s2: Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting an item from the cart
- s3: Button to execute the delete
- s4: Button to cancel the delete

Constraints:
- s1: max 24 characters
- s2: max 16 characters
- s3: max 8 characters (including punctuation)
- s4: max 8 characters

And they explicitly say "JSONのみを返してください" (Return only JSON), so I must reply with only the JSON object, nothing else — no explanation before or after. The character count constraints presumably count Japanese characters (including punctuation like ！？、). Let me draft candidates.

s1 (max 24 chars): Empty cart message. Common phrasing: 「カートに商品が入っていません」— let me count: カ, ー, ト, に, 商, 品, が, 入, っ, て, い, ま, せ, ん = 14 characters. Good. Since there's already a "商品を探す" button at the bottom, maybe add a hint pointing to it? But the button already exists so a simple statement works. Could also be 「カートは空です」 (7 chars). The message 「カートに商品が入っていません」 is natural and standard. 14 chars ≤ 24. 

Alternatively 「カートに商品がありません」= 12 chars. Both fine. I'll go with 「カートに商品が入っていません」.

s2 (max 16 chars): Title of delete confirmation dialog. Options:
- 「商品を削除しますか？」= 商,品,を,削,除,し,ま,す,か,？ = 10 chars. Good.
- 「カートから削除しますか？」= 12 chars.
- 「商品を削除しますか」= 9 chars without question mark.

The title of a dialog typically doesn't need the question mark; the question usually goes in the body. But we only have title specified. Since we only have a title slot, making it a question works as a combined title. Actually, in Japanese mobile apps, dialog titles are often short nouns like 「削除の確認」(5 chars) or 「商品の削除」(5 chars). Hmm. Since the requirement says "確認ダイアログのタイトル", a typical title would be 「削除の確認」or 「商品を削除しますか？」.

Let me think: The dialog presumably has title + maybe body + two buttons (delete/cancel). Since only the title is requested, I could make the title carry the question. But it's safer/more standard to have a noun title like 「削除の確認」 (5 chars). However, if the dialog body isn't asked for, maybe the design only includes the title and buttons, in which case the title should be the question. Hmm.

Actually for Japanese dialogs, if there's no separate body text, the title often becomes the question: 「カートから商品を削除しますか？」= カ,ー,ト,か,ら,商,品,を,削,除,し,ま,す,か,？ = 15 chars ≤ 16. That fits within 16! Good option too.

But a title of 15 chars is long. A more common pattern: title 「削除の確認」 with body asking. But body isn't in scope. I'll choose something that works as a standalone title: 「商品を削除しますか？」(10 chars). Hmm, but as a "title" it's a bit unusual. Many Japanese apps do use question titles though.

Let me decide: s2 = 「商品を削除しますか？」 — 10 chars. This is safe within the limit and clearly conveys the confirmation. Alternatively 「削除しますか？」(7 chars) — but ambiguous about what's deleted. I'll keep 「商品を削除しますか？」.

Wait — with buttons s3 「削除する」 and s4 「キャンセル」, the title question + buttons works fine.

s3 (max 8 chars): Delete button. 「削除する」= 4 chars. Good. Or 「削除する」. 
s4 (max 8 chars): Cancel button. 「キャンセル」= 5 chars (キ,ャ,ン,セ,ル). Good.

Counting: "キャンセル" has 5 characters. ≤ 8. Good.

The counts likely include the full-width question mark as one character. All within limits.

Final JSON:
{"s1":"カートに商品が入っていません","s2":"商品を削除しますか？","s3":"削除する","s4":"キャンセル"}

Let me double check character counts:
s1: カ(1)ー(2)ト(3)に(4)商(5)品(6)が(7)入(8)っ(9)て(10)い(11)ま(12)せ(13)ん(14) = 14 ≤ 24 ✓
s2: 商(1)品(2)を(3)削(4)除(5)し(6)ま(7)す(8)か(9)？(10) = 10 ≤ 16 ✓
s3: 削(1)除(2)す(3)る(4) = 4 ≤ 8 ✓
s4: キ(1)ャ(2)ン(3)セ(4)ル(5) = 5 ≤ 8 ✓

Output only JSON, no code fences? The instruction says "JSONのみを返してください". I should output raw JSON without markdown fences to strictly comply. The user said return only JSON. I'll output plain JSON text.</think>{"s1":"カートに商品が入っていません","s2":"商品を削除しますか？","s3":"削除する","s4":"キャンセル"}
